In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transduction of the signal from the GnRH receptor is a complex process involving multiple intracellular mediators and pathways, and that these mediators are likely to act in concert to bring about the release of the gonadotropins.
GnRH stimulates GTH release in the tilapia by activating adenylate cyclase and phospholipase C, and the resultant increase in cAMP and Ca2+ leads to the stimulation of GTP release.

GnRH stimulates the release of GTH from tilapia pituitary cells via a mechanism involving the activation of adenylate cyclase, mobilization of intracellular Ca2+, activation of protein kinase C and the generation of arachidonic acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

GnRH action in tilapia is mediated by a cascade involving Ca2+ influx from extracellular and intracellular sources, mobilization of Ca2+ from intracellular pools, activation of PKC and adenylate cyclase, and arachidonic metabolism.
GnRH action is transduced by a complex mechanism involving multiple signal transduction pathways in tilapia.
GnRH stimulates the release of gonadotrophin (GTH) in teleosts through a mechanism involving calcium, protein kinase C, and arachidonic acids.

GnRH action on tilapia GTH release is mediated through the same transduction cascades as those found in mammals, birds, reptiles, amphibians and other teleosts.
